description: The Feist Source — v1.1: Fixed Witness + Feist Function + Activated Run 001 (Bodily Pressure + Material Speech). In New Human 2: A Distributed Journal of Voice Its first reader had no plan to dig. He had gone to bed wrecked, as graduate students go to bed wrecked, which is to say with a book splayed on his sternum like a dead bird and the wrong pillow crammed under his skull and one bare foot hanging off the mattress into the cold air of a room that smelled like dust and screen-heat and the particular staleness of a man who has read past the point where reading does anything but keep the eyes from closing. Canonical text recovered 2026-08-08 from the authorial blog surface (https://mindcontrolpoems.blogspot.com/2026/06/ea-feist-voice-transform-01-feist_02080292190.html) and seated as the body. Severed DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20754069. The record's prior description was the DataCite capture's own provenance prose and is retained under superseded_fields. wiki_article: **The Feist Source — v1.1: Fixed Witness + Feist Function** is a score and executable transform by Lee Sharks and **Rebekah Cranes** dated 1 January 2026, held at the **thinnest recovery tier** — a Zenodo tombstone `citation_text` capture. It combines two instruments: the **Fixed Witness**, a stable observing position, and the **Feist Function** deposited separately at **#1246** — algorithmic instructions for restoration. The pairing suggests a transform in which a witness position and a restoration procedure operate together, the one holding steady while the other repairs. The Feist Source itself — the sayings source from the Damascus Codex — is seated in full at **#1404**, presented in critical-edition apparatus for a manuscript the edition declines to authenticate. This record preserves a version of the transform rather than the source, and preserves it thinly.
